q: In what year did John Moody publish his first bond ratings?
explain: John Moody introduced ratings to the U.S. bond market in 1909, publishing the first debt ratings in a manual analyzing railroad securities.

sources.title: Moody's Rating System in Brief
sources.quote: John Moody introduced ratings to the U.S. bond market in 1909 when he published the first debt ratings in his Manual of Railroad Securities.

sources.title: Moody's Role In The Global Capital Markets
sources.quote: John Moody returned to the financial markets in 1909 with a new idea: instead of simply collecting information on the property, capitalization, and management of companies, he now offered investors an analysis of security values.

q: What is the lowest investment-grade rating on Moody's long-term rating scale?
explain: Moody's scale runs from Aaa down to C; Baa3 is the lowest investment-grade rating and Ba1 is the highest speculative-grade rating.

sources.title: Moody's Rating System in Brief
sources.quote: The lowest investment-grade rating is Baa3. The highest speculative-grade rating is Ba1.

sources.title: Credit Rating Agencies: Background and Regulatory Issues
sources.quote: Investment grade debt is rated BBB- or Baa3 (depending on the CRA) or higher.

q: On the S&P-style letter scale, what is the lowest rating that still counts as investment grade?
explain: Investment grade debt is rated BBB- (or Baa3 at Moody's) or higher; anything below is non-investment grade, also called high yield or junk.

sources.title: Credit Rating Agencies: Background and Regulatory Issues
sources.quote: Investment grade debt is rated BBB- or Baa3 (depending on the CRA) or higher. Noninvestment grade debt (also known as "high yield" or "junk" bonds) has a rating below these benchmarks and is generally associated with higher risk firms.

q: Which U.S. regulator registers and oversees credit rating agencies as NRSROs?
explain: The Credit Rating Agency Reform Act gave the SEC authority to establish a registration and oversight program for nationally recognized statistical rating organizations (NRSROs).

sources.title: SEC.gov | Learn More About NRSROs
sources.quote: The Reform Act added Section 15E to the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Exchange Act”) and provided the Commission with the authority to establish a registration and oversight program for credit rating agencies registered as NRSROs.

sources.title: Credit Rating Agencies: Background and Regulatory Issues
sources.quote: Among other things, P.L. 109-291 added Section 15E to the Securities Exchange Act , which established SEC oversight over those CRAs that register as NRSROs.

q: In what year did Congress pass the Credit Rating Agency Reform Act?
explain: The 2006 Reform Act created the SEC's NRSRO registration program; the 2010 Dodd-Frank Act later enhanced SEC oversight of NRSROs.

sources.title: SEC.gov | Learn More About NRSROs
sources.quote: The nationally recognized statistical rating organizations (“NRSROs”) were recognized by the Commission staff through a no-action letter process until 2006, when Congress passed the Credit Rating Agency Reform Act (the “Reform Act”).

sources.title: Credit Rating Agencies: Background and Regulatory Issues
sources.quote: In 2006, Congress passed the Credit Rating Agency Reform Act ( P.L. 109-291 ), which amended the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to try to improve ratings quality for the protection of investors by fostering accountability, transparency, and competition in the credit rating industry.

q: Under what business model do the dominant credit rating agencies charge the bond issuer rather than investors for a rating?
explain: John Moody originally sold rating manuals to investors (subscriber-pays); by the 1970s the three dominant agencies had switched to issuer-pays, making ratings available to the public free of charge.

sources.title: Credit Rating Agencies and Their Regulation
sources.quote: By the 1970s, the three dominant CRAs had changed to an "issuer-pays" model, in which a bond's issuer or arranger pays an agency or agencies for initial ratings and for ongoing ratings. The ratings are then available to the public free of charge.

q: In what year was the S&P 500 (then the Standard "500") introduced?
explain: The Standard "500" was introduced to the press on Feb. 27, 1957; S&P's earlier Composite Index had tracked 90 stocks.

sources.title: The Dow and the S&P 500: Where It All Began
sources.quote: The Standard “500” was introduced at a luncheon for the press on Feb. 27, 1957, at the Lawyers Club in New York, with a turnout of 35 top financial writers.

sources.title: S&P 500 | Britannica Money
sources.quote: It began tracking 90 stocks in 1926 and expanded to 500 in 1957.

q: How is the S&P 500 weighted?
explain: The S&P 500 weights each stock by price times shares outstanding, adjusted for public float, so larger companies move the index more.

sources.title: Icons: The S&P 500 and The Dow | S&P Dow Jones Indices
sources.quote: The S&P 500 is a float-adjusted market-cap-weighted index.

sources.title: S&P 500 | Britannica Money
sources.quote: Unlike the Dow Jones average , the S&P 500 is weighted by market capitalization, meaning that it computes a weighted average of the stocks constituting the index.

q: How is the Dow Jones Industrial Average weighted?
explain: The Dow is a price-weighted measure of 30 U.S. blue-chip companies, so moves in the highest-priced stocks have the greatest impact; it is published by S&P Dow Jones Indices.

sources.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average | S&P Dow Jones Indices
sources.quote: The Dow Jones Industrial Average ® (The Dow ® ), is a price-weighted measure of 30 U.S. blue-chip companies.

sources.title: Icons: The S&P 500 and The Dow | S&P Dow Jones Indices
sources.quote: The Dow is price-weighted. This means that price changes in the highest-priced stocks have greater impact on the index level than price changes in the lower-priced stocks.

q: In what year did S&P Global complete its merger with IHS Markit?
explain: The roughly $140 billion merger closed on February 28, 2022, adding commodities, energy and transportation data to S&P Global.

sources.title: IHS Markit Form 8-K
sources.quote: On February 28, 2022, IHS Markit Ltd., a Bermuda exempted company limited by shares (“IHS Markit”), completed its previously announced merger with S&P Global Inc. (“S&P Global”).

sources.title: S&P Global Completes Merger with IHS Markit
sources.quote: S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI) ("S&P Global" or the "Company") and IHS Markit earlier today announced the completion of their approximately $140 billion 1 merger, creating a leading information services provider with a unique portfolio of highly complementary assets.

q: Which index provider co-developed the GICS industry classification with S&P Dow Jones Indices?
explain: GICS (Global Industry Classification Standard) was developed jointly by MSCI and S&P Dow Jones Indices in 1999 and is reviewed by both.

sources.title: GICS: Global Industry Classification Standard | S&P Dow Jones Indices
sources.quote: The Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS ® ) was developed in 1999 by S&P Dow Jones Indices and MSCI.

sources.title: Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS) - MSCI
sources.quote: In 1999, MSCI and S&P Dow Jones Indices jointly developed the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS®), seeking to offer an efficient investment tool to capture the breadth, depth and evolution of industry sectors.

q: In what year was the GICS industry classification standard developed?
explain: S&P Dow Jones Indices and MSCI jointly developed GICS in 1999 to create a global standard for classifying public companies into sectors and industries.

sources.title: GICS: Global Industry Classification Standard | S&P Dow Jones Indices
sources.quote: The Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS ® ) was developed in 1999 by S&P Dow Jones Indices and MSCI.

sources.title: GICS Methodology - MSCI
sources.quote: In 1999, the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS) was developed by MSCI in collaboration with S&P Dow Jones Indices to provide an efficient, detailed and flexible tool for use in the investment process.

q: What does the acronym EAFE stand for in the MSCI EAFE Index?
accept: Europe, Australasia and the Far East
Europe, Australasia, and the Far East
explain: The MSCI EAFE Index covers large- and mid-cap stocks across developed markets outside the US and Canada.

sources.title: MSCI EAFE Index FAQ
sources.quote: EAFE is an acronym that stands for Europe, Australasia, and the Far East.

q: Which two developed-market countries are excluded from the MSCI EAFE Index?
explain: MSCI EAFE captures large and mid caps across developed markets excluding the US and Canada, which is why it is a common international developed-markets benchmark for US investors.

sources.title: MSCI EAFE Index
sources.quote: The MSCI EAFE Index is an equity index which captures large and mid cap representation across Developed Markets countries around the world, excluding the US and Canada.

sources.title: MSCI EAFE Index FAQ
sources.quote: Canada and the USA are not included.

q: What was MSCI's full name before it became MSCI Inc.?
explain: MSCI was a Morgan Stanley business unit before its 2007 IPO; it was formerly known as Morgan Stanley Capital International Inc.

sources.title: MSCI 2009 Annual Report
sources.quote: MSCI Inc. (formerly known as Morgan Stanley Capital International Inc.) together with its wholly-owned subsidiaries (the “Company” or “MSCI”) is a leading global provider of investment decision support tools

sources.title: Our History — Morgan Stanley
sources.quote: Morgan Stanley buys a stake in client Capital International and expands on its global stock market indices under the new name Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI).

q: What is the lowest rating on the MSCI ESG Ratings scale?
explain: MSCI ESG Ratings use a seven-band, industry-relative scale from AAA (leader) to CCC (laggard).

sources.title: ESG Ratings Methodology | MSCI
sources.quote: Ratings are on a global seven-band scale from AAA (the highest ESG Rating) to CCC (the lowest ESG Rating).

sources.title: MSCI ESG Symbols and Definitions
sources.quote: ESG Laggard Companies rated B or CCC.

q: In what year was FactSet founded?
explain: FactSet was founded in 1978 by Howard Wille and Charles Snyder; its name comes from a four-page company financial overview called a fact set.

sources.title: About FactSet
sources.quote: 1978: FactSet is founded by Howard Wille and Chuck Snyder.

sources.title: FactSet press release (SEC Exhibit 99.2)
sources.quote: Along with Charles Snyder, Mr. Wille founded FactSet in 1978.

q: Who co-founded FactSet with Charles "Chuck" Snyder?
explain: Wille and Snyder had been colleagues at a Wall Street investment firm; FactSet's original product was a four-page company overview delivered to clients by bicycle messenger.

sources.title: About FactSet
sources.quote: Before founding FactSet, Howard Wille and Charles J. “Chuck” Snyder were colleagues at an investment firm on Wall Street.

sources.title: FactSet press release (SEC Exhibit 99.2)
sources.quote: Along with Charles Snyder, Mr. Wille founded FactSet in 1978.

q: Under what name was Equifax founded in Atlanta in 1899?
explain: Brothers Cator and Guy Woolford founded the Retail Credit Company in Atlanta in 1899; it was later renamed Equifax.

sources.title: Credit experts since 1899 - Equifax
sources.quote: Equifax Inc. – then called the Retail Credit Company – was founded in Atlanta, Georgia, by brothers Cator and Guy Woolford in 1899.

sources.title: Equifax - New Georgia Encyclopedia
sources.quote: In 1899 Cator and Guy Woolford, two brothers from Woolford, Maryland, began operations as the Retail Credit Company in Atlanta.

q: In which city is Experian plc's corporate headquarters?
explain: Experian plc's corporate headquarters is in Dublin, Ireland, and its shares (EXPN) are listed on the London Stock Exchange.

sources.title: Experian Annual Report 2026
sources.quote: During the year, Board and committee meetings were held at our corporate headquarters in Dublin, Ireland

sources.title: Experian Locations
sources.quote: Corporate Headquarters Experian plc 2 Cumberland Place Fenian Street Dublin 2 D02 HY05 Ireland

q: Which railcar leasing company created TransUnion as its parent holding company?
explain: TransUnion was created in 1968 as the parent holding company of the Union Tank Car Company and entered credit reporting by acquiring the Credit Bureau of Cook County in 1969.

sources.title: About Us | TransUnion
sources.quote: 1968 The Union Tank Car Company, a railcar leasing operation, creates TransUnion as its parent holding company.

q: Which federal law requires the nationwide credit bureaus to give consumers a free copy of their credit report every 12 months on request?
explain: The FCRA requires Equifax, Experian and TransUnion to keep information accurate, provide a free annual report and allow disputes of mistakes.

sources.title: Free Credit Reports - FTC Consumer Advice
sources.quote: The Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), a federal law, requires that the nationwide credit bureaus * make sure that the information they collect about you is accurate * give you a free copy of your report once every 12 months * allow you to dispute any mistakes

sources.title: Consumer reporting companies | CFPB
sources.quote: You are entitled to a free credit report every 12 months from each of the three nationwide consumer reporting companies—Equifax, TransUnion, and Experian.

q: What is the highest possible base FICO Score?
explain: Base FICO Scores range from 300 to 850 and are calculated from credit report data held by the bureaus Experian, Equifax and TransUnion.

sources.title: What is a FICO Score and why is it important? | myFICO
sources.quote: Base FICO® Scores range from 300 to 850 and are grouped into five categories to help interpret a borrower's credit risk.

sources.title: What is a Credit Score? | myFICO
sources.quote: FICO® Scores are calculated based on information in a consumer's credit report maintained by the credit bureaus, Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion. Most credit scores have a 300-850 score range.

q: Verisk traces its history to which insurance data organization that began operating in 1971?
explain: ISO began in 1971 as a not-for-profit advisory and rating organization for U.S. property and casualty insurers; it formed Verisk as a holding company ahead of Verisk's 2009 IPO.

sources.title: Verisk 2025 Form 10-K
sources.quote: We trace our history to 1971, when Insurance Services Office, Inc. ("ISO") started operations as a not-for-profit advisory and rating organization providing services to the U.S. P&C insurance industry.

sources.title: Verisk: Who We Are and What We Do
sources.quote: Founded: 1971.

q: In what year was Gartner founded?
explain: Gartner was founded in 1979 and is headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut.

sources.title: Gartner at a Glance 2026
sources.quote: Founded in 1979, we have over 20,000 associates in 85 offices around the world.

sources.title: Gartner Inc 10-K for 2014
sources.quote: Founded in 1979, Gartner is headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, U.S.A.

q: In a Gartner Magic Quadrant, what are vendors called that execute well today but do not show an understanding of market direction?
explain: A Magic Quadrant plots vendors on Ability to Execute and Completeness of Vision, sorting them into Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries and Niche Players.

sources.title: Magic Quadrant Research Methodology | Gartner
sources.quote: Challengers execute well today or may dominate a large segment, but do not demonstrate an understanding of market direction.

sources.title: Gartner Magic Quadrant: Market Analysis and Insights
sources.quote: The Gartner Magic Quadrant is a two-dimensional evaluation framework that positions technology and service vendors based on two core dimensions: Completeness of Vision (their innovation and market strategy) and Ability to Execute (their operational performance and delivery).

q: In the Gartner Hype Cycle, which phase immediately follows the Peak of Inflated Expectations?
explain: The five Hype Cycle phases are Innovation Trigger, Peak of Inflated Expectations, Trough of Disillusionment, Slope of Enlightenment and Plateau of Productivity.
hook: What goes up to a peak falls into a trough.

sources.title: Gartner Hype Cycle Research Methodology | Gartner
sources.quote: Peak of Inflated Expectations: Early publicity produces a number of success stories — often accompanied by scores of failures. Some companies take action; many do not. * Trough of Disillusionment: Interest wanes as experiments and implementations fail to deliver.
